authorNotes: All productions, venues and events are fictional. The transport comparison and material donation deliberately create different overlapping bridge pairs.

captures.rationale: An explicit single touring undertaking spans two venues.
captures.text: Paper Birds autumn tour: one production visits Moss Hall and Reed Theatre with the same cast and folding set. Venue adjustments stay within this tour.

captures.rationale: A distinct production remains separate despite sharing the play title.
captures.text: Next spring's Paper Birds studio revival is separately commissioned. New director, new fixed set, its own rehearsal budget; it is not another autumn tour stop.

captures.rationale: The workshop has its own client, participants and deliverable.
captures.text: Youth centre booked a standalone shadow-theatre workshop. Build small practice screens and finish with each group presenting a scene.

captures.rationale: A bicycle repair has no supported theatrical connection.
captures.text: Bicycle repair photo: rear rim is buckled beside two broken spokes. Record spoke length before rebuilding and tensioning the wheel.

captures.rationale: One estimate compares two productions without making them one project.
captures.text: Transport estimate compares the Paper Birds autumn folding set with next spring's studio-revival set. Same haulier, separate collection dates and job numbers.

captures.rationale: Venue-specific adaptation remains within the defined tour.
captures.text: Reed Theatre stop of the autumn tour: fold the left panel inward for the narrow wing. Keep the Moss Hall arrangement in the same touring cue book.

captures.rationale: Several theatre projects use screens, and neither audience nor production is named.
captures.text: Make the screen taller; they cannot see the bird.
Reed Theatre autumn-tour rehearsal clip: the revised left-panel fold clears the wing, and the touring bird silhouette remains visible from the back row.

captures.rationale: Resolves the ambiguous screen instruction to the workshop.
captures.text: The taller-screen memo is for the youth shadow workshop's practice screens. The children need to see the bird over the table edge.

captures.rationale: A material-transfer source spans revival and workshop, not the autumn tour.
captures.text: Material handover: offcuts from the separately built Paper Birds studio-revival set will make the youth workshop's practice screens. Record the donation against both projects.

captures.rationale: Review of both stops closes the one touring production.
captures.text: Autumn tour closed after Reed Theatre. The inward panel fold worked; preserve both venue configurations in the Paper Birds touring report.

captures.rationale: Records the workshop result; mentioning donated materials does not itself make this a revival progress report.
captures.text: Youth shadow workshop recording: the taller practice screens made from revival offcuts let each group perform its bird scene without lifting the tables.

challenges: One tour spans venues, but a separately commissioned revival stays separate.
Two overlapping bridges form a chain without authorizing a three-project merge.
A workshop can reuse production material while remaining its own undertaking.
Generic screen language leaves three plausible project referents.

events.text: Reed Theatre stop of the autumn tour: fold the left panel inward by 30 degrees for the narrow wing. Keep the Moss Hall arrangement in the same touring cue book.

events.reason: c09 identifies the screen-height memo as a youth workshop instruction. Assign it to that standalone workshop.
